name: Session Drift Continuation (intraday, opening window)
hypothesis: Institutional orders get worked over multiple days, so yesterday's net buying or selling pressure persists into today's open. A session that closed near the high of the opening window on heavy volume (net drift) predicts the same direction in the next session's opening window.

_intake_answers.hypothesis: Institutional orders get worked over multiple days, so yesterday's flow persists into today's open. (User selected this mechanism explicitly from the offered options.)
_intake_answers.universe: Equities (US ETFs, sectors, international) narrowed by the user to Broad ETFs only: SPY/VTI/IVV/RSP = the us_equity_broad preset.
_intake_answers.entry: Previous session's net drift = where it closed within its range, times volume.
_intake_answers.exit: Flat at the 10:00 close of the window - no overnight risk.
_intake_answers.rebalance: Every session (daily). Derived from the user's own statement that the strategy 'only trades on the open of the new york session 9:30 to 10:00'.
_intake_answers.costs: Same as daily-bar defaults, no adjustment.
_intake_answers.period: DATA-CONSTRAINED. The user was informed that Yahoo 60m history is capped at roughly 2 years, so only one window exists. Pinned to the first available session (2024-10-24) and run to the last (2026-10-23). Recorded as a finding rather than asked as a choice.
_intake_answers.variants_tried: 1 - the user stated they did not really tune it.

intake.notes: All 12 conditions supplied by the user via the intake questionnaire. Limitations carried into the report: (1) gamma exposure and order-flow data are NOT available in this engine, so the hypothesis is tested through its net-drift component only - the mechanism the user named (worked institutional orders) is proxied by close-location-in-range x volume; (2) only about 2 years of 60m history exists, capping statistical power; (3) 4 instruments with a 10% cap and a quartile split yields at most 1 long + 1 short, so realised gross is 0.2x, not the stated 1.0x; (4) intraday costs use daily-bar cost defaults at the user's request, which is likely optimistic for an opening-window strategy. These conditions deliberately match the engine's default value (universe, direction, entry, costs), so they are recorded in accepted_defaults. They are still the USER's answers, not the engine's - but if you keep any of them, say so deliberately rather than by omission.

answers.A.asset_classes: IN SCOPE: US broad ETFs only (SPY/VTI/IVV/RSP), long and short. EXCLUDED: FX, crypto, futures, bonds/credit, commodities, options, individual stocks, international equity. The user narrowed a broader 'equities' scope down to broad ETFs.
answers.A.rationale: Single asset class in scope, so no cross-class combination rationale applies. Signal rationale: institutional orders get worked over multiple days, so yesterday's net flow persists into today's open.
answers.A.universe_rules: Static list of 4 broad ETFs. NOT point-in-time. ETFs sidestep the delisting survivorship bias that individual equities would carry, which is why they were selected.
answers.A.rebalance_horizon: Every session (daily). Signal horizon: the previous session only (1 day). Holding period: one opening window (09:30-10:00 ET), flat by the close.
answers.A.allocation: Inverse-volatility sizing (equal risk contribution) within the 4-instrument universe, normalised to gross 1.0x, then capped at 10% per instrument. VERIFIED FINDING: the 10% cap binds on every single bar, so every realised weight is exactly +/-0.10 and the inverse-vol sizing is COMPLETELY INERT - it cannot affect the result. The user's stated sizing method was not actually exercised.
answers.A.constraints: Gross 1.0x target, max 10% per instrument. VERIFIED FINDING: with 4 instruments and a top/bottom-quartile split (1 long + 1 short), the 10% cap binds every bar, so realised gross is 0.2x, not the stated 1.0x. Sharpe is leverage-invariant so the verdict is unaffected, but the CAGR and drawdown reported are 5x smaller than a 1.0x book would show. Consequence: the inverse-volatility sizing the user specified never took effect.
answers.A.direction: Long and short (directional). Top quartile long, bottom quartile short.
answers.G.variants_tested: 1 - the user stated they did not really tune it.
answers.A.rejection_criteria: NOT SPECIFIED BY THE USER - recorded as UNKNOWN. Pre-registered rejection criteria were never set, which weakens the falsifiability of this test.
answers.A.benchmark: NOT SPECIFIED BY THE USER - UNKNOWN. No investable benchmark was named, so performance is measured against zero net-of-cost expectancy instead of against an investable alternative.
answers.A.null_hypothesis: Zero net-of-cost expectancy, and no marginal diversification benefit from any asset class. NOTE: the second half is NOT tested - the engine does not perform leave-one-asset-out.
answers.E.commissions: Same as the engine's daily-bar cost defaults, no adjustment (the user's explicit choice). Flagged in the report as likely optimistic for an opening-window strategy, where spreads are typically wider.
answers.D.asset_selection: The user narrowed the universe from all US equities to broad ETFs BEFORE the test was run, and no asset class was added or removed after seeing results.
answers.I.forward_test_type: Not yet started. The engine is retrospective only; forward testing is a separate manual process.
